payload.reason: Attempt 1 was taken back for one reason: fork O-017 needed a measurement. Spike 107 has answered it with YES on three valid Sandbox sets, so the design is rewritten on that answer and on the spike's constraints. The bug report gave only a title. The working assumption is the captured SC-130 failure, which the slice text, the build check and the repro already pin down in detail; nothing else had to be assumed. The build check said 'a person should rescope before design starts'. This design does that rescoping itself. The loop-runnable harness fix and the outcome-C record stay in this slice. Both Restart sessions go to a person, and the measurement-preparation work goes to a later slice.
payload.selection_rationale:
There was one proposal (practice), and it is taken as the core. It was checked against what the survey and the spikes measured.

1. Backlog item 3 is mostly moot in the tree. The R_start 2 GiB abort and the empty-L.json judge lived only in the scratch ScanArm/Protocol.cs, which was never committed (git ls-files and git log --diff-filter=D). The tree's PoolWatch.ps1 already has a per-arm guard: 6 GiB over the arm's own /before mark, or Available under 3 GiB. It still writes /exit and the 10-minute /settled mark after a stop (:347-365). What is left of item 3 is SC-130.

2. The SC-130 fix is the reorder spike 106 proved (sc130-guard-stop-survives-interrupt-fix, go). The repro passes in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, and 8 fixture cases print identical output.

3. Spike 107 answered O-017 YES on A-small, A-large and FileRepository H1: warm probe repeats net NtfF +0/+0/+0, accumulation is +4/+5/+5, and the WC leak tags stay within idle. So there is no listing-only arm and no new Invoke-Protocol arm type.

4. Spike 107's binding constraints are designed in:
- NtfF counts folders, not files, so Ntff joins the deciding tags.
- Tags are keyed case-exactly everywhere: an Ordinal Get-Net dictionary, a fitness rule, and a variant-first fixture.
- Sandbox protocols must fit the 1,800 s ceiling; that goes to the measurement-preparation slice.

5. The investigation's cause (L's growth is Windows' file-system metadata cache, about 1 per cold folder, about 0 warm) and spike 106 shape the record and the tag list:
- A standby purge re-created 0% of NtfF on VHD.
- Deep pressure frees the cache, but only shown at Sandbox scale.
- The 15 named tags cover 85.4% of paged growth, under 90%, with NtFs at 5.1% unnamed.
So there is no purge or pressure step, more tags are recorded, and the product is not changed.

6. The practice designer raised over_engineering_flag, and it is honoured. There is no judge, no tolerance row, no ScanArm and no listing arm. The record is read by a person, and fitness.yaml:1097 keeps verdict words out of the harness.

7. Lessons #344 and #357: every Restart and whole-C: run is filed for a person, not built.

Changes made to the proposal, each against a measurement or an answered decision:
- WC leak tags are judged against their own idle movement only, not max(idle, 10% of F1). Spike 107's own WC criterion was idle-only, Q-178(1) says WC* +0, and lesson #349's +5 per walk has to stay visible.
- The spike evidence goes under docs/design/SL-099-runs/. The proposal named both SL-095-runs and SL-099-runs. Q-184 keeps DONE (c) session logs alone in SL-095-runs.
- The seven WC leak tags are appended to :66 if absent. It is not known that HEAD records WCse, WCss and WCfn, and the rule decides on them.
- The warm set is generalised to 'the F arms after the first Completed F arm'.
- Y3 is resolved as wanted and carried to the measurement-preparation slice.
- guardAtStart arms are explicitly excluded from the new guard branch.
- Every unchanged fixture's -Report output is compared with HEAD's.
- The fitness patterns get a $null lookahead and a switch pattern, and are scoped to PoolWatch.ps1.

components.name: Get-Missing guard-stop branch
components.responsibility:
Branch order in Get-Missing:
1. The guardAtStart branch (:459) stays first. Cascade arms also carry guardStop ('available N MB at start').
2. Next, an arm with guardStop set and guardAtStart not set is judged by the guard branch. The interrupted branch (:460-465) comes after it.

The guard branch needs /before and /exit with non-null pagedBytes and nonpagedBytes. It prints ONE line per arm: '  MISSING arm <X>: stopped by the machine guard (<reason>): paged ±N MiB, nonpaged ±N MiB from /before to /exit'. If either mark or either field is missing, the net is replaced by 'its net at the stop is unread (no <mark> mark | <mark> <field> is null)'.

If the arm was interrupted, a suffix is worded from the marks that exist:
- '; then interrupted before its /exit mark' when there is no /exit;
- '; then interrupted before its /settled mark' when /exit exists and /settled does not (the repro's shape);
- '; then interrupted after its /settled mark' when all three exist (a throw in the report read at :366-380, after /settled at :365);
- ' and killed' is appended when killed is true.

If the arm was not interrupted, HEAD's /settled presence check and its four field checks (:466-472) still run, each with its own line.

The old guard branch at :473-478 can no longer be reached and is removed. Interrupted arms without a guardStop keep :460-465 byte for byte.
components.key_interactions: Calls Get-Net (:512-520). Write-RunReport is unchanged: its table still shows X1 with status 'guard' and '(no net: a mark is missing)', because the table reads /before to /settled. Strings are ASCII only, and none match \b(PASS|FAIL|VOID|OUTCOME)\b (.taad/fitness.yaml:1097). No new function. Exit 2 for an incomplete run is unchanged.

Append to the named tag list at :66 every name below that is not already there, checked with -ccontains at build time:

- MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, NtxI, Ntfo, Ntff, NtxF, NtFs, FSim, MmSm, Ntf0, MmRe, Ntce.

Read-Mark's -ccontains (:207) and Tag()'s -ceq (:242) stay as they are. Get-Net builds its result (:515-516) as New-Object System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary ([StringComparer]::Ordinal). The non-tag keys (paged, nonpaged, handles, h120089) keep HEAD's spelling. $NetTags (:67) and the -Report columns are unchanged.
components.key_interactions: An Ordinal dictionary makes every reader's key spelling matter. The build greps every reader of Get-Net's result (Write-RunReport :559 and the guard branch) and makes their spelling match exactly. Case 8 diffs each unchanged fixture's -Report output against HEAD's to catch a miss. Marks keep NtfF and Ntff, and NtxI and NtxF, as separate entries. The committed build-2026-10-05 marks already list Ntff ahead of NtfF, so any hand reader must match case-exactly; the record says so.

components.name: Case-exact tag comparison rule
components.responsibility:
One entry over tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 holding the four patterns under architecture_rules. It is the engine-appended attempt-1 entry at .taad/fitness.yaml:1176-1178, extended by hand into a single entry, never a second copy.

Corpus:
- Must fire: `Where-Object { $_.tag -eq $name }`, `Where-Object tag -eq $t`, `$WatchedTags.Where({ $_ }) -contains $_.tag`-style `-contains $_.tag`, `switch ($row.tag) {`.
- Must stay quiet: `$_.tag -ceq $name`, `-ccontains $_.tag`, `$tag -eq $null`, `switch -CaseSensitive ($row.tag) {`.

The rule must report 0 hits on HEAD's PoolWatch.ps1. If it hits, the hit is either a real case-folding comparison, which this slice fixes, or a pattern defect, which is fixed before acceptance.
components.key_interactions: Plant rows go in eng/rules-harness/plants.json if the harness can plant into a .ps1, and are run with harness.py --only <ids> (lesson SL-089). Otherwise the build runs Fitness on a scratch copy with the fire lines planted and records what it prints. The engine does not replace a same-named rule that persists across take-backs (lesson SL-091), so the build edits the file and checks that no duplicate was appended.

components.name: P-003 guard-and-interrupt fixture arms
components.responsibility:
New arms, alongside the unchanged X3, F2 and F4:
- (b) The criterion's shape: guardStop 'available 2900 MB, pool +310 MiB over <arm>/before', exitCode -1, interrupted true, killed false, /before and /exit present, no /settled. Asserts the reason, 'paged +310 MiB' with 'from /before to /exit', and '; then interrupted before its /settled mark'.
- (c) guardStop with interrupted true, killed true, exitCode null and no /exit mark. Asserts 'its net at the stop is unread', '; then interrupted before its /exit mark and killed', and the absence of 'from /before to /exit'.
- (d) guardStop, not interrupted, all three marks, but /settled has pagedBytes null. Asserts the guard line with its net AND a separate line naming /settled pagedBytes.
- (e) guardStop, interrupted true, killed false, all three marks present. Asserts '; then interrupted after its /settled mark'.

components.name: P-004 tag-recording case

Added to the ValidateSet (:17) and the All list (:375).

Fixture half:

Live half:

- Reads the live pool tag table once, then one Read-Mark. Asserts that every oracle name present in the live table is present in the mark with the same live count source.

components.name: Outcome-C redesign record
components.responsibility:
The O-028 redesign for outcome C (backlog item 1, SC-128's design). Sections:

(a) Outcome C stands, by pointer to SL-095 doc :11-15. The tens-of-GB report is not claimed fixed, and Q-188 stays open.

(b) The cause of L's growth, as investigated. Windows keeps file-system metadata for each cold folder listed: NtfF, NtxI, Ntfo, FMfn, FMsl, FIcs, File, MmSt, MmCa.
- About 800 B per folder over 669,824 directory opens.
- About 0 on a warm repeat (spike 106 listing; spike 107 full probe).
- Freed by deep memory pressure at Sandbox scale only (spike 106).
- Not reliably freed by a standby purge: 0% of NtfF re-created on VHD (spike 106).
MS Q&A 5966064 is quoted: about 1 KB per cold path, and 24.4 GB combined (10,786 MB nonpaged) after 47.41 h with no release. So the cache explanation does not close Q-188.

(c) What the old criterion measured. T = 64 MiB and the 0.5 GB guard counted reclaimable cache. 'L stopped by the guard' does not show a leak. Spike 87's pool deltas and tag growth cannot be checked now: only L.json, dirs-count.txt and skips.log survive.

(d) The reading rule for the person's session-1 logs.
- Series: F1..F5 on the same root (Invoke-Protocol :609). The warm set is every F arm after the first one whose status is Completed. Fewer than two warm arms decides nothing.
- Per tag, d is the live-count change from /before to /settled. Accumulation is measured from the first warm arm's /settled to the last warm arm's /settled.
- NtfF (per folder) and Ntff (per file; spike-107 constraint): bound = max(the largest same-length |movement| over I0/I1, 10% of F1's rise).
- WCsc, WCse, WCss, WCfc, WCri, WCfn, FMwi: bound = that tag's own largest same-length idle movement, with no F1 term.
- A leak reading is a tag over its bound on two or more warm arms, or an accumulation over its bound.
- Reported but not deciding: FMfn, File, MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, NtxI, Ntfo, NtxF, NtFs, FSim, MmSm, Ntf0, MmRe, Ntce, Toke, FMfc.
- F1's absolute cost is reported next to Q-188 and not judged against any tolerance.
- Until the -Report reader lands, Ntff, WCse, WCss and WCfn are read case-exactly from marks.jsonl.

(e) Preconditions:
- Same workload: holds (:609).
- A warm full-probe repeat nets about 0: holds at Sandbox scale (spike 107). SC-230 and O-016 are discharged.
- F1 is cold: must-verify.
- F1's cache survives until F2..F5: must-verify.
The record says what breaks if either must-verify fails.

(f) Spike-107 limits:
- 4 GB RAM, at most 400,000 files, ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.1;
- I1 skipped or trimmed, so 600 s idle pairs were not measured (SC-241);
- 0 reparse and 0 sparse files;
- the Sandbox's C: is wcifs-backed (P1 WCsc +961).
An F1 WC rise on the host is not to be explained away (Q-178(1)).

(g) Disposition table: one '| <id> | settled here|carried|dropped | reason |' row each.
- Settled here: M6 and N2 (same-length idle bound), M3, N3 and X2 (no purge or pressure step; warm repeats discriminate), ScanArm (does not return).
- Dropped: M2 (no listing arm), M4 and Y1 (unfixed afd021d arms).
- Carried to the measurement-preparation slice: R3-1, R4-1, X5, N1, Q-185, steps 3-5, the cancel trigger, and Y3. Y3 is wanted because (d) makes a WC-within-idle claim (SC-129's condition).

(h) Scope split: two person-run Restart sessions, with logs in docs/design/SL-095-runs/ per Q-184, and the measurement-preparation slice.

components.name: SL-095 hand-off pointer
components.responsibility: One line in the hand-off section (:219-229) pointing to docs/design/SL-099-outcome-c-redesign.md and its disposition table. Nothing else in that document changes.

key_decisions.decision: Get-Missing judges a guard stop (guardStop set, guardAtStart not set) after the guardAtStart branch and before the interrupted branch. It writes one line per arm, worded from the marks that exist. A guard-stopped arm that was not interrupted still gets HEAD's /settled checks.
key_decisions.rationale: This is the reorder spike 106 proved: the repro passes in 5.1 and 7, and 8 fixture cases are identical. A fixed 'before its /settled mark' wording would be false for an interrupt before /exit and for a throw after /settled (:365-380). guardAtStart arms carry guardStop too, so a guard-first branch placed ahead of :459 would report every cascade arm as 'net unread'.

key_decisions.decision: Fork O-017 is resolved YES from spike 107. Invoke-Protocol gets no listing-only repeat arm. The measurement-preparation slice's listing-arm clause (M6) is dropped. SC-230 and O-016 are discharged with the three runs cited and committed.

The reading rule decides on NtfF and Ntff with bound max(same-length idle |movement|, 10% of F1's rise). It decides on the seven WC leak tags against their own idle movement only. It reads the F arms after the first Completed F arm and needs at least two of them.
key_decisions.rationale:
Spike 107: NtfF rose once per folder (+401 for 400 folders plus the root) and had 0 allocations across 400,000 SizeProbe opens. Ntff carries the per-file state (+13,180 cold, then +48/-72/+44 against b = 1,318).

The proposal applied the 10% term to WC tags as well. That would hide a per-pass WC leak whenever F1's WC rise exceeds about 50. It contradicts spike 107's own WC criterion (idle only), Q-178(1) (WC* +0), spike 87's harness (allowance 0 for the leak tags), and lesson #349 (+5 per walk is what the rule must see).

A guard-stopped F1 leaves the next arm partly cold. Changing the rule after session 1 costs another Restart.

key_decisions.decision: The tag list at :66 gains the 14 names and any of the seven WC leak tags that are absent. Read-Mark and Tag() stay case-exact as they are. Get-Net's result becomes an Ordinal OrderedDictionary. $NetTags and the -Report columns are unchanged.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 106 measured the 15 named tags covering 85.4% of paged growth, with NtFs at 5.1% unnamed, and spike 107 recorded these names. The rule decides on WCse, WCss and WCfn, which HEAD may not record. Spike 107 read NtfF 917 against Ntff 15,895 in one mark. [ordered]@{} would fold them together the moment the measurement-preparation slice adds Ntff to $NetTags.

key_decisions.decision: The harness's tag comparisons are guarded by one fitness entry over tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1. It has four patterns (operators on a tag, -contains/-in against a tag, $_[0] comparisons, and a switch on a tag without -CaseSensitive), a $null lookahead, a fire/quiet corpus, and a 0-hit gate on HEAD. It extends the attempt-1 entry rather than adding a copy.
key_decisions.rationale: The entry as appended cannot see Tag()'s `$_.tag -ceq $name` turning into `-eq`, and that comparison decides the NtfF column. Lessons SL-096 and SL-075: run a corpus before trusting a regex. `$tag -eq $null` is correct code and must stay quiet. Lesson SL-091: same-named appended rules persist and are not replaced.

key_decisions.decision: P-004 proves tag recording with a variant-first fixture, a literal spelling oracle and one live Read-Mark. A mutation of :242 to -eq must turn it red. No C-052 run is added.
key_decisions.rationale: Tag() returns the first match, so a fixture that lists NtfF first passes even with case folding. A misspelled watched name is absent from the live table and gets skipped silently. One live read takes about 0.4 s. C-052 costs about 5 min and +0.11 GB against the engine's 0.5 GB whole-machine guard (lesson #351).

key_decisions.decision: PoolWatchCases.ps1 roots every fixture through Get-ScratchParent, so it runs under the engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
key_decisions.rationale: Lesson #391 lists PoolWatchCases.ps1 as red under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, leaving folders only an administrator can list. The build check's 9-green run recorded no TEMP. This slice's P-003 and P-004 have to pass in the engine's validate.

key_decisions.decision: No change to src/: Scanner.cs, DirectoryReader.cs, KnownWorkarounds.cs and the precaution text stay byte-identical. No new KnownWorkarounds entry.
key_decisions.rationale: The investigation found that L's growth is Windows' designed metadata cache, which the app does not step around: it lists each folder once, as any listing tool does. That is not an outside defect worked around, so the one-checkbox-per-bug rule adds no entry. The wcifs WC* leak is a real outside defect, and it is still answered by the existing 'wcifs-layer-store' entry (Q-186), which stays as built. Per Q-183, the Q-004 rule stays.

key_decisions.decision: Spike 107's evidence is committed under docs/design/SL-099-runs/. The person's DONE (c) session logs stay in docs/design/SL-095-runs/.
key_decisions.rationale: Backlog item 4 shows what happens otherwise: spike 87's marks.jsonl and events.log were lost and its pool figures are now uncheckable. One spike-107 run folder sits outside the worktree. Q-184 puts SL-095's DONE (c) logs in SL-095-runs only.

Lessons #344 and #357: a Restart plus whole-C: runs cannot close on loop evidence, and the engine's guard forbids them unattended. The fork no longer needs an arm before session 1, so nothing in the split waits on SC-230.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Selected whole, with seven seams redesigned (see coherence_check). over_engineering_flag was raised and is honoured: no judge, no tolerance row, no purge or pressure step, no listing arm, no ScanArm.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there was no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement, and the reviewer should treat all of it as uncontested.

The pieces were checked against each other, against the spikes and against the answered questions. Seven seams were redesigned:

1. WC bound. The proposal bounded every deciding tag by max(idle, 10% of F1). Spike 107's WC criterion was idle movement only, Q-178(1) says WC* +0, and spike 87's harness gave the leak tags an allowance of 0. Changed: WC leak tags are bounded by their own idle movement only.

2. Evidence path. The proposal's component named both SL-095-runs and SL-099-runs. Changed to SL-099-runs, which also keeps Q-184's rule that DONE (c) logs live alone in SL-095-runs.

3. Deciding tags that may not be recorded. The rule decides on WCse, WCss and WCfn, but HEAD's :66 is not known to record them; the survey wrote 'WC*' and review m1 said there is no WC* family. Changed: the seven WC leak tags are appended if absent, and P-004's oracle covers them.

4. Key spelling. Moving Get-Net to an Ordinal dictionary makes every reader's key spelling load-bearing. Added: a diff of each unchanged fixture's -Report output against HEAD's (case 8).

5. Cascade arms. guardAtStart arms also carry guardStop. Made explicit: the new branch excludes guardAtStart and runs after :459 (case 3, C-056).

6. Partly cold repeats. m7's 'F3..F5 if F1 guard-stopped' is generalised to 'after the first Completed F arm, at least two'.

7. Y3. SC-129's condition is resolved: the rule makes a WC-within-idle claim, so Y3 is wanted and carried, not built.

Contradictions checked and found consistent:
- Q-178, Q-184 and Q-185 are compatible with the reading rule and the session split.
- Q-183 and Q-186 are untouched, because there is no product change.
- fitness.yaml:1097 still holds: there is no verdict word because there is no judge.

A conflict between two measurements, which the design avoids rather than resolves:
- The investigation's Sandbox standby purge freed big-folder state.
- Spike 106's purge re-created 0% of NtfF on a VHD 400x40 set.
The design uses neither purge nor pressure as a discriminator.

Backlog item 3's R_start abort has no counterpart in the tree; the survey measured that the faulty ScanArm was never committed. The record says so and nothing is built for it.

decidable_disagreements is empty. The one fork that could force a re-synthesis (O-017) was settled by spike 107. What remains is either cheap, so the build settles it (the 0-hit fitness gate, whether the spike folders still exist), or person-only (host-scale behaviour, filed).

One architecture rule is declared: case-exact tag comparison in PoolWatch.ps1. Its glob matches an existing file. It is to be merged into the attempt-1 entry by hand, because the engine does not replace a same-named rule (lesson SL-091).

architecture_rules.name: PoolWatch compares pool tags case-exactly
architecture_rules.because: NtfF and Ntff, and NtxI and NtxF, differ only by case. Spike 107 read NtfF 917 against Ntff 15,895 in one mark. PowerShell's -eq, -contains, -in, -like, -match and switch fold case by default. One folded comparison puts one tag's count in the other's column, and the outcome-C reading rule decides on NtfF and Ntff. A wrong column in the person's session-1 logs costs another true Restart.

cases.shape: Stopped by the guard, then interrupted during its settle wait after the exe exited (exit -1, killed false). /before and /exit present, no /settled. This is the repro's X1 and P-003 arm (b).
cases.why: Get-Missing tests interrupted at :460-465 and continues before reaching guardStop at :473, so the guard's reason and the +310 MiB /before-to-/exit net are dropped. This is the captured failure.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-099-GuardStopSurvivesInterrupt.Tests.ps1 exits 0, and powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-099-GuardStopSurvivesInterrupt.Tests.ps1 exits 0. Also pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 exits 0 (arm b).

cases.shape: Stopped by the guard and not interrupted, with all three marks present (the repro's control X2).
cases.why: Moving the guard branch ahead of the field checks could drop X2's net, split it into two lines, or skip its /settled checks.
cases.check: The same repro run as in case 1 (its X2 checks) exits 0. pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case C-056 exits 0.

cases.behaviour: report an arm the guard refused at start
cases.shape: A guardAtStart cascade arm. It also carries guardStop ('available N MB at start') and has no /exit mark.
cases.why: Placed ahead of :459, a guard-first branch would report every cascade arm as 'stopped by the machine guard ... its net at the stop is unread' and lose 'cascade from X'.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case C-056 exits 0, and its -Report text equals the same case run on a git worktree of 0feac0e.

cases.shape: Stopped by the guard, then interrupted before its /exit mark, while the exe was still being killed (killed true, exitCode null).
cases.why: The net needs /exit. The suffix must not claim an /exit that does not exist, and the killed flag changes the wording.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 exits 0, with arm (c) asserting 'its net at the stop is unread' and '; then interrupted before its /exit mark and killed', and no 'from /before to /exit'.

cases.shape: Stopped by the guard, all three marks written, then interrupted by a throw in the report read after /settled (:366-380).
cases.why: A fixed 'before its /settled mark' suffix would be false. The marks-derived suffix has a third branch.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 exits 0, with arm (e) asserting '; then interrupted after its /settled mark'.

cases.shape: Stopped by the guard and not interrupted, but its /settled mark has a null pagedBytes.
cases.why: The guard branch needs only /before and /exit. Without HEAD's /settled field checks kept for non-interrupted arms, a failed reading would go unreported.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 exits 0, with arm (d) asserting the guard line with its net and a separate line naming /settled pagedBytes.

cases.shape: Interrupted with no guard stop, either while the exe ran (killed) or after it exited 0 (P-003's F2 and F4).
cases.why: The interrupted branch must stay byte for byte for arms without a guard stop.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 exits 0, and its F2/F4 lines equal the same case run on a git worktree of 0feac0e.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Leak testing in managed runtimes (repeat an identical workload after a warm-up and check whether retained growth scales with the number of passes)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Tell a leak from a cache by the slope across identical warm repeats, not by one pass against an absolute tolerance. The counter being read must actually see the objects each pass creates.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Spike 107 confirmed the slope half on the app's real Scanner with ScanOptions.Default, on three cold sets. It also showed this pattern's usual trap: a counter blind to a pass's objects reads 0 whether there is a leak or not. NtfF counts folders, so the per-file reading goes to Ntff. The forced-reclaim half does not transfer (spike 106: a purge re-created 0% of NtfF on VHD). This synthesis adds one point: a counter with a known per-pass leak signature (WC) must not be given a bound that scales with the cold pass.

invariants.precondition: The repetitions are the same workload.
invariants.evidence: Invoke-Protocol :609 passes the same root, the exe-full type and a null hook to every F arm.

invariants.precondition: A warm full-probe repeat nets about 0 on the deciding tags, with no accumulation.
invariants.evidence: Spike 107 on three valid sets: NtfF +0/+0/+0, accumulation +4/+5/+5, P2 exit+600 +1 to +3, Ntff on A-large +48/-72/+44 against b = 1,318, WC within idle on every warm repeat. Sandbox scale only: 4 GB RAM, at most 400,000 files, ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.1.

invariants.precondition: The judged counter sees the objects each pass creates.
invariants.evidence: It fails for NtfF on files: +401 for 400 folders, and 0 allocations across 400,000 SizeProbe opens. Ntff is added to the rule because it churned 23-27k allocations per warm pass at a flat live count.

invariants.precondition: The bound does not grow with the cold pass for a counter whose leak signature is a small per-pass rise.
invariants.evidence: In this design, WC leak tags are bounded by idle movement only (spike 107's WC criterion; Q-178(1)). Lesson #349's +5 WC per walk stays above an idle movement of 2-9.
-Protocol refuses to start more than 30 min after boot (:690-691). Background services may warm parts of C: first, which only makes F1 look smaller.

invariants.precondition: The cache F1 builds survives to F2..F5.
invariants.evidence: The host has about 17 GB of standby memory, and the 6 GiB per-arm guard and 3 GB floor keep the run away from deep pressure. If the cache were evicted, the warm repeats would rebuild it and read as a leak; the record says so.

invariants.precondition: A forced-reclaim step reliably frees the cache.
invariants.evidence: Spike 106: a standby purge re-created 0% of NtfF on a VHD set. Deep pressure released the cache only at Sandbox scale (SC-231).

prior_art.pattern: Find a pool leak by watching per-tag pool bytes and allocations over time (PoolMon).

Cold first-time opens keep about 1 KB of pool per path, and warm paths add nothing. On a 32 GB PC the same tags reached 24.4 GB combined pool (13,626 MB paged, 10,786 MB nonpaged) after 47.41 h and were cleared only by a reboot. This is evidence for the cache mechanism, and also that it can reach the size of Q-188's growth without being given back.
Killing the triggering process tree does not release the FltMgr/File pool it caused, so a reading taken after exit measures Windows' state.
Take a baseline of normal pool usage before attributing growth to a tag.
Iterate an identical workload after warm-up and flag retained growth that scales with the number of iterations.
prior_art.where: LeakCanary / dotMemory Unit / Valgrind memcheck practice

prior_art.pattern: PowerShell's -eq, -contains, switch, @{} and [ordered]@{} ignore case by default. Case-exact work needs -ceq/-ccontains, switch -CaseSensitive, or a [StringComparer]::Ordinal collection.

outside_claims.claim: PowerShell's -eq, -ne, -like, -match, -contains, -in, switch, @{} and [ordered]@{} compare strings case-insensitively unless the c-prefixed operator, switch -CaseSensitive or an Ordinal comparer is used. This holds in both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7.
outside_claims.if_wrong: If PowerShell compared case-exactly by default, the fitness rule would only be noisy, and the Get-Net change would be unneeded but harmless.

outside_claims.claim: System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary has a constructor taking an IEqualityComparer, and New-Object ... ([StringComparer]::Ordinal) reaches it under both .NET Framework 4.x (5.1) and .NET (pwsh 7).
outside_claims.if_wrong: Get-Net needs another ordered Ordinal map, for example a Dictionary[string,object] with Ordinal plus a separate key list. P-004 and case 8 would show the failure at build.

outside_claims.claim: NtfF rises once per folder listed and does not see per-file SizeProbe opens. Per-file NTFS state shows on Ntff.
outside_claims.source: spike 107 sandbox-above-cap-warm-probe-repeat-ntff: +401 for 400 folders plus the root, 0 NtfF allocations across 400,000 probes, Ntff +13,180 (Sandbox, ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.1)
outside_claims.if_wrong: If host ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.9444 assigns the tags differently, the reading rule's choice of Ntff as the per-file counter is wrong. Session 1's F1 rise would show it: Ntff flat while files are probed.

outside_claims.claim: A warm repeat of a full default-ProbeRule scan nets about 0 on NtfF, Ntff and the WC leak tags, with no accumulation.
outside_claims.source: spike 107, three valid sets (A-small, A-large, FileRepository H1)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Warm repeats would not separate cache from leak, and a listing-only repeat arm would be needed before session 1 (the fork's NO branch).

outside_claims.claim: A standby purge does not reliably make listed folders cold again, while memory pressure deep enough to drain the standby list releases the listing state.
outside_claims.source: spike 106: sandbox-purge-repeat-attribution-combined (no-go, 0% NtfF re-created on VHD) and sandbox-deep-pressure-releases-listing-state (go, Sandbox)
outside_claims.if_wrong: A purge step could become a cheaper discriminator. Nothing built here depends on it.

outside_claims.claim: The 15 originally named tags cover 85.4% (77.1% in run 2) of a cold listing's paged growth, with NtFs at 5.1% unnamed.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Only the reported-tag list grows. The deciding tags are unaffected.

outside_claims.claim: Cold first-time path operations keep about 1 KB of pool per path. The same tag family reached 24.4 GB combined after 47.41 h on a 32 GB PC and was cleared only by reboot.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The record's statement that the cache explanation does not close Q-188 would lose its outside support. The design does not change.

outside_claims.claim: Killing the process that triggered FltMgr/File pool growth does not release that pool.
outside_claims.if_wrong: A /settled reading would partly measure the app rather than Windows. The rule's after-exit window would need rethinking.

outside_claims.claim: SystemPoolTagInformation and the pool counters are readable unelevated on this PC in about 0.4 s.
